text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: At the midpoint of the Kavuru Valley Farmer Field School Initiative, the evaluation team visited 24 of the 40 active schools between March and May 2023. Facilitators had trained roughly six hundred farmers in compost preparation and intercropping, and 68% of interviewed participants reported adopting at least one new practice on their own plots. Women made up just over half of regular attendees. However, the seed multiplication component did not meet its targets, because the planned community seed bank in Lumeza was never built. Farmers in upland groups said that extension officers rarely visited after the first season. The team recommends shifting two facilitators to upland schools and agreeing a revised timetable for the seed bank before the 2024 planting season.

passages.source_passage: During the reporting period of 1 July to 30 September 2024, the Tembera District Net Campaign distributed 18,450 long-lasting insecticidal nets across 112 villages. Distribution teams registered households the week before each event, and community health volunteers hung demonstration nets in schools and clinics. Spot checks in a sample of 300 homes found that 81% of nets were hanging over a sleeping space. Some families did not use the nets during the hot months, citing heat and a lack of hooks. In three fishing villages, nets were reportedly being used to dry fish, and no follow-up visit had yet taken place there. The monitoring team will prioritise these villages in October and add hanging kits to the next consignment.

passages.source_passage: By the end of the second quarter of 2024, the Sunflower Steps network was running 36 community playgroups in Marisol and Upper Dene, each meeting twice a week. Attendance registers show an average of fourteen children per session, up from eleven in January. Caregivers lead songs, storytelling and counting games, while trained facilitators observe and record each child's progress. Not all groups have safe outdoor space, and four playgroups in Upper Dene still meet in borrowed church halls without toilets. Developmental screening was not completed for 22% of enrolled children because the screening tool arrived late. Facilitators expect to close this gap before the September review.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Lantern Hours evening literacy programme covered 18 classes in the river towns of Osra and Belcamp. Of the 410 learners enrolled in 2022, about 290 were still attending eighteen months later, a retention rate of roughly 71%. Most learners can now read short notices and write their own names and addresses. Volunteer tutors reported that solar lamps donated by the Belcamp Traders' Association made late sessions possible. Nevertheless, learners over sixty did not progress as quickly as younger classmates, and the numeracy module was never adapted for people with poor eyesight. The evaluators found no evidence that certificates were being recognised by local employers.

passages.source_passage: In 2023, with support from the Halvorsen Fund, the Dry Lands Harvest project distributed sorghum, cowpea and pearl millet seed to 1,250 households in the Qarsa plateau. Rainfall was 35% below the ten-year average, yet farmers who planted the drought-tolerant varieties harvested nearly twice as much grain as neighbours using local maize. Twelve lead farmers hosted demonstration plots and field days attended by more than nine hundred visitors. The planned rainwater harvesting ponds were not finished, as contractor costs rose sharply after June. We have not used any of the contingency budget and propose reallocating it to complete three ponds before the 2024 rains.

passages.source_passage: Throughout 2024, the Common Table cash transfer programme made monthly payments of 45 dollars to 3,200 households in the Nemba and Sorro districts. Payments were sent by mobile money on the fifth day of each month, and only two monthly cycles were delayed, both because of network outages. Our household survey in November found that 74% of recipients ate at least two meals a day, compared with 52% at baseline. Recipients did not report pressure from local traders to spend transfers in particular shops. However, households headed by older people were not always able to reach agents, so we introduced home delivery for 140 of them in August.

passages.source_passage: Session 3 of this guide prepares volunteers for their first home visits with scholarship families in San Ignacio de las Lomas and the surrounding hamlets. Each volunteer will support up to eight scholars, meeting them at least once a month. Since the programme began in 2019, 214 girls have received scholarships, and 9 out of 10 have stayed in school through the end of each year. Volunteers should never promise families extra money or goods beyond the published scholarship package. If a scholar misses more than five school days in a month, do not confront her in front of relatives; instead, speak to her privately and inform the field coordinator within 48 hours.

passages.source_passage: In the first half of 2025, caregivers with the Ubuhle Home Care Circle completed 2,640 home visits to 315 clients living with HIV in Kwanyoni township. Each visit includes a check on medication adherence, a wellbeing conversation and, where needed, wound care. Viral load results were available for 188 clients, and 87% of those were virally suppressed. Fifteen clients missed clinic appointments for more than two months, and caregivers were not able to trace six of them. Stock of gloves and dressings ran out twice in April. No caregiver reported a needle-stick injury during the period, but supervisors noted that refresher training on infection control hasn't been held since 2023.

passages.source_passage: This update covers case management at Block C of the Hadiri settlement from January to March 2025. Our team of nine caseworkers opened 164 new protection cases, most involving unaccompanied children and survivors of gender-based violence. Around 40% of cases were referred by community watch groups rather than by partner agencies. Waiting times for a first interview fell from twelve days to five after we added evening shifts. The team did not have a private interview room until February, and some survivors declined to speak in the shared tent. The board is asked to approve funding for a second room, as the current space is not sufficient for confidential work.

passages.source_passage: In 2024, the Saltmarsh Signals programme extended its early-warning network to 27 coastal villages along the Brenna peninsula, funded by the Ostrander Foundation. Volunteers installed 54 sirens and trained village response committees to run evacuation drills twice a year. When Cyclone Ilse made landfall on 14 October, warnings reached 92% of registered households at least six hours in advance. No deaths were recorded in programme villages, although two fishing boats were lost at sea. Four sirens did not sound during the storm because their backup batteries had not been replaced. We have since added battery checks to the monthly maintenance schedule and will not rely on mains power alone.
